profile.research_note:
Correction pass 2026-09-03, batch 99 followup (Stack Infrastructure): a post write comparison against the generated source file for this row found a preexisting technical_space_sqft value of 182,000 already on file from before this session, identically duplicated across all 4 POR03 rows in this registry, which this session generator script had not touched since it never included that key in its own payload. Given this session own fresh research confirms 6 real distinct buildings on the POR03 campus with differing square footage, an identical figure across 4 rows is not credible as 4 separate building measurements, so the field is removed rather than left in place implying false precision, and reading updated to document the correction.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-03] This facility is attributed in the registry to Stack Infrastructure, or in 3 Milan, Italy rows researched in this same batch, to the shorter operator field spelling STACK. This batch researches both spellings together since both point to the operator branded stackinfra.com in sources fetched this session, but this batch does not merge or rewrite either operator field value, leaving that naming inconsistency on file for a future pass to resolve if desired. STACK Infrastructure was launched January 16, 2019, per a trade press article from datacenterdynamics.com fetched this session, by IPI Partners, described in that article as a joint venture between Iron Point and Iconiq Capital. The new company launched with eight data centers across six United States markets and about 100 MW of capacity, built from two predecessor portfolios, three facilities from Infomart Data Centers in Ashburn Virginia, Portland Oregon, and Silicon Valley California, which IPI Partners had acquired in March 2018 after Equinix bought Infomart own Dallas headquarters building earlier that year, and five facilities from T5 Data Centers, a company IPI Partners had separately backed since 2016, in Atlanta Georgia, Chicago Illinois, and the Dallas Fort Worth Texas area, with T5 Data Centers itself continuing to operate separately afterward with remaining sites in Los Angeles, Charlotte, Colorado Springs, New York, and Cork City Ireland. Brian Cox, previously chief executive of Infomart Data Centers, became STACK Infrastructure own chief executive. STACK Infrastructure own about page, fetched this session, describes the company as a partner designing, developing, and operating global digital infrastructure, and states a current footprint of 10 metro markets in the Americas, 5 in Asia Pacific, and 7 in EMEA, 22 markets in total, though each market can itself include multiple campuses, for example Silicon Valley alone contains 3 campuses and Milan alone contains 11. This registry already carried, prior to this session, one already complete row for an Atlanta, Georgia facility a prior pass in this registry had itself corrected from an operator field of T5 Data Centers to Stack Infrastructure based on a documented 2019 sale, and one already complete row for the New Albany, Ohio facility, one of the original eight launch data centers, both consistent with the acquisition history recorded here and both untouched by this batch. None of the operator own pages fetched this session for the facilities in this batch published a street address, so no row in this batch receives an address field, a reverse geocoding attempt on one representative coordinate this session was again throttled, consistent with a persistent throttle on that service observed repeatedly earlier in this same campaign. This row is one of 4 rows in this registry that all carry the identical name Stack Infrastructure - POR03 and the identical operator own website URL, at coordinates within about 250 meters of one another. The operator own dedicated page for POR03, fetched this session, describes a 55 acre campus with 6 buildings, POR03A through POR03F, and 200 MW of total critical capacity, made up of 72 MW of operational critical capacity, 25 MW with near term availability, and 96 MW of expansion capacity, with individual building square footage ranging from 180,000 to 530,000 square feet, the largest, POR03E and POR03F, at 530,000 square feet with 96 MW. Because the real campus independently confirmed on the operator own page has 6 distinct buildings, a number close to the 4 rows this registry carries for POR03, this batch treats these 4 rows as most plausibly corresponding to 4 of the 6 real distinct buildings on a single shared campus rather than as duplicate OSM mappings of one building, unlike a smaller cluster of exact duplicate pairs found and marked as such in a recent prior batch for a different operator in this registry. No single building capacity or square footage figure can be attributed to any specific one of these 4 rows from the operator own campus level page fetched this session, so none is added to any of them, and no duplicate_of relationship is recorded among them. A post write check this same session found this row already carried a technical_space_sqft figure of 182,000 square feet from a pass earlier than this session, and found the identical 182,000 figure duplicated across all 4 of the POR03 rows in this registry. Given the operator own page fetched this session confirms 6 real, physically distinct buildings on this campus with individually differing square footage from 180,000 to 530,000 square feet, 4 different real buildings sharing one identical figure is implausible, so this session removes that preexisting figure from this row rather than let 4 rows imply 4 buildings of exactly the same size on the strength of a figure this session cannot verify against any specific one of them. No new square footage figure is substituted, since this session likewise cannot confirm which specific one of the 6 real buildings this row corresponds to.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure POR03 in Hillsboro, Oregon has 200 MW of total critical capacity across a 55-acre campus with 6 buildings, but only 72 MW is operational today and 25 MW is available for near-term deployment.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 97 MW of operational plus near-term capacity would support roughly 2,400 racks. Oregon has published capacity of 156.6 MW across 8 mapped facilities. POR03's operational and near-term capacity represents 62 percent of the state's total disclosed capacity. The state contains 133 mapped facilities in OpenStreetMap, but only these 8 have published capacity figures, so POR03 is one of very few Oregon sites with a disclosed spec.

The site publishes no power interconnection details, grid connection status, or compliance certifications. Whether the 97 MW of current and near-term capacity can actually be energized depends on grid headroom and power availability that are not documented here. The 96 MW of expansion capacity depends on permitting, construction, and grid allocation decisions that the published spec does not address.
